compiled_state.title: [.test-index]: non-runnable yaml/config files allowed as test targets -> spurious 'command not found' failures
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** worktree-20260506-183119 HEAD
* **Discovered:** 2026-05-07 during /dso:debug-everything autonomous bug-fix session, while editing plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/anti-patterns.md (bug 6ee4-652f).

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** Sub-Agent Blocker

#### Expected Behavior

`.test-index` entries should reference RUNNABLE test files (bash scripts, python pytest modules, etc.). The pre-commit test gate runs each entry as a test, so non-runnable file types should never appear as test runners.

#### Actual Behavior

`.test-index` line for plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/anti-patterns.md mapped to TWO targets:
1. plugins/dso/hooks/semgrep-rules/test-anti-patterns.yaml (a semgrep RULES config — not runnable)
2. tests/scripts/test-fix-bug-anti-pattern-step.sh (legitimate test)

When the test gate ran the yaml as bash, output was a series of "command not found" errors:

```
plugins/dso/hooks/semgrep-rules/test-anti-patterns.yaml: line 1: rules:: command not found
plugins/dso/hooks/semgrep-rules/test-anti-patterns.yaml: line 4: -: command not found
plugins/dso/hooks/semgrep-rules/test-anti-patterns.yaml: syntax error near unexpected token `('
```

The test gate counted this as a failure and blocked the commit until I removed the yaml entry from .test-index manually. There is no validation that .test-index entries point to executable files.

### 3. Action History

* Filed during the same /dso:debug-everything session that fixed bug 6ee4-652f. Removed the yaml entry inline as collateral; ticket created here to track the underlying gap (no entry-validation guard).

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* plugins/dso/scripts/check-test-index-duplicates.sh (existing dedup guard — could host this check)
* .test-index format spec
* Suite-engine readers (bash-runner, pytest selector)

#### Suggested fix scope

Extend check-test-index-duplicates.sh (or a sibling pre-commit hook) to validate that each .test-index test target is one of: a `.sh` file with the executable bit set, or a `.py` file matching `test_*.py` / `*_test.py`. Reject entries that match a known non-runnable extension list (`.yaml`, `.json`, `.md`, `.conf`). The check is essentially free (path inspection only) and the false positive rate should be near-zero given the existing convention.

NOTE: this bug requires intent-alignment investigation before fix. The .test-index format may legitimately allow non-runnable entries for documentation purposes — verify before adding rejection logic.
